newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rapeseed tops higher German 1995/96 crush data.
newsitem.headline: Rapeseed tops higher German 1995/96 crush data.

text.p: German oilseeds crushers processed 3.64 million tonnes of rapeseed in July/June 1995/96, 13 percent more than in the same 94/95 period, rounded figures from the Bonn farm ministry showed on Monday.
Total crushings were 7.61 million tonnes, up from 7.48 million in the previous campaign.
Much of the boost in rapeseed was due to the higher 1995 area planted to seed for industrial use on set-aside land.
Rape oil from such areas is used in fuel, oleochemical and hydraulics applications, but production this year is down and will fall further as the EU has cut the land set-aside rate.

Rapeseed crushings in 95/96 accounted for 48 percent of the crush versus 43 percent a year earlier, while soybeans accounted for 42 percent in 95/96, down from 45 percent a year earlier, the ministry said.
The total crush produced 2.40 million tonnes of vegetable oils (2.28 million 94/95) and 5.17 million tonnes of meals and cakes (5.12).
The remainder of the total covers production losses and wastage.
The oil total included 1.51 million tonnes of rapeseed oil (1.31 million).
